subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should redirect persistence failure remain fail-closed—suppressing the source notice even when the operator-session write fails—or should OpenClaw define a recoverable retry or fallback contract?
rationale: This is a user-visible privacy and availability tradeoff. The patch can implement either path, but code review cannot decide whether avoiding source disclosure outweighs guaranteed operator visibility for every deployment.

options.title: Approve fail-closed redirect
options.body: Keep the source chat suppressed when writing the operator-session notice fails, prioritizing non-disclosure of operational details.

options.title: Define recoverable delivery
options.body: Specify a bounded retry, durable operator alert, or explicitly opt-in fallback contract, then adjust the implementation and prove both failure and recovery paths.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed redirect
recommendation.body: Keep the source chat suppressed when writing the operator-session notice fails, prioritizing non-disclosure of operational details.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice changes the core privacy boundary and public configuration contract across all supported delivery paths.
